lesson.text: Quick memory: who are the people who help us? (Doctors, nurses, firefighters and police officers.) Today: how to call for help in an emergency.
An emergency is when someone is badly hurt or very ill, when there is a fire, or when someone is in danger right now.
First, look around: is it safe for you to go near? If it is not safe, stay back and shout for a grown-up.
Call {number}. A calm helper answers. Say what happened and where you are, and answer their questions.
Learn your address with your grown-up and say it out loud. If you don't know it, say what you can see nearby. Never type it into a game.
Stay with the person, and keep the phone on until the helper says goodbye. Help is on its way.
Try it in the world: open the practice room and help Bobo the buddy. Next: first aid for cuts and burns, on the Middle track.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is an emergency?
choices: someone is badly hurt and cannot get up
exercises.explain: Someone badly hurt needs help fast: that is an emergency.

exercises.prompt: Before you help, you check it is safe for you.
exercises.hint: Think about what you do first.
exercises.explain: True: check it is safe first, so nobody else gets hurt.

exercises.hint: Someone is there to help, day and night.
exercises.explain: A calm helper answers and asks you questions, so the right help comes.

exercises.prompt: You type your address into a game.
exercises.hint: Your address is something you say out loud to the right person.
exercises.explain: False: say your address out loud to a grown-up or to the emergency helper. Never type it into a game.

exercises.prompt: Put calling for help in order.
exercises.hint: Safety first, and staying with them last.
exercises.explain: Check it is safe, call {number}, say what happened and where, then stay with them.

exercises.prompt: The helper asks where you are, and you don't know your address. What can you say?
exercises.hint: What would help them find you?
exercises.explain: Say what you can see: a big shop, a park, a school, a sign.

exercises.prompt: Call for help, or not an emergency?
exercises.hint: Is someone hurt, ill or in danger right now?
exercises.explain: Smoke and someone who won't wake up need help now. A lost toy and a pencil can wait.

exercises.prompt: When you have said what happened, you hang up at once.
exercises.hint: Who says when the call can end?
exercises.explain: False: keep the phone on until the helper says goodbye.

exercises.prompt: Bobo fell, and his leg hurts. He is awake and talking. What do you do?
choices: call for help and stay with him
exercises.hint: Bobo needs help, and a friend beside him.
exercises.explain: Call for help and stay with Bobo until help comes.

exercises.prompt: Why do you stay on the phone?
choices: the helper tells you what to do
exercises.hint: The helper knows what to do.
exercises.explain: The helper tells you what to do while help is on its way.

exercises.prompt: Emergency numbers are only for real emergencies.
exercises.hint: What if a joke call kept the helpers busy?
exercises.explain: True: a joke call could stop help reaching someone who really needs it.

exercises.prompt: You see smoke coming from a house. Put it in order.
items: go far away from the house
exercises.explain: Go far away from the house, tell a grown-up, and call {number}.
